message.content:
Yes—if you’re experiencing excessive or disruptive noise in Atlanta, you can file a formal complaint with the city’s authorities. Here’s how you can do it:

| Step | What to Do | Contact Details |
|------|------------|-----------------|
| **1** | Identify the source and time of the disturbance. | — |
| **2** | Call the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line at **404‑656‑4000** (or dial 311 from within the city). | 404‑656‑4000 |
| **3** | If the issue involves a commercial establishment or a residential building, you may also contact the City of Atlanta’s Code Enforcement Office. | 404‑656‑4000 (same number) |
| **4** | Alternatively, submit a written complaint online through the City of Atlanta’s official portal. | https://www.atlantaga.gov/ |
| **5** | For persistent or severe cases, you can file a formal complaint with the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (GEPD) if the noise violates state environmental regulations. | 404‑656‑4000 |

### Quick Tips

* **Non‑Emergency Line:** Use 404‑656‑4000 for anything that isn’t urgent. This line will connect you to the appropriate department (code enforcement, police, etc.).
* **Online Form:** The city’s website offers a “Noise Complaint” form under the “Public Safety” section. Fill out details such as address, description, and time of the disturbance.
* **Documentation:** Keep a record of dates, times, and any evidence (audio recordings, photos, witness statements) to support your claim.
* **Follow‑Up:** After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Use this when following up with the city or police.

If you’re unsure which department to contact, start with the non‑emergency line; the dispatcher will direct you to the correct agency. Good luck!
